coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: The Beacon
record.summary: Two residential towers at 250 and 260 King Street, for which the Department of Building Inspection filed new-construction permits in November 2000 (17 stories each; 279 and 307 dwelling units) and recorded both as completed on 2004-10-06; the Assessor roll gives 2004 as year built for the condominium lots at 250 King Street, and two listing sites give 595 residential units and Catellus as developer.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL -- surveyed OpenStreetMap building footprint(s), not a hand trace or plan estimate. The underlying Assessor parcel is condo-mapped across many individually owned per-unit lots (confirmed against DataSF's Assessor parcel data), so no single blklot represents the whole building and it cannot be mapped from one parcel the way a single-owner building can. Using the real building footprint from OSM instead of a fabricated or arbitrarily chosen 'representative' unit lot, the same real-geometry-without-a-single-parcel pattern already used for several Pier 70 buildings (DataSF Building Footprints) and for Mission Bay's own real park polygons.

The map notes now set out what the listing sites do and do not say about units, developer and the conflicting architect credits.

open_questions: Developer is stated only by a listing site (SFHighrises); the Catellus Mission Bay page cited in the map's geometry file does not mention The Beacon. No primary source read confirms it.
Architect not recorded: Afi + Associates says Skidmore, Owings and Merrill; other attributions seen earlier by the project are unsourced here.

The permits do not use the name 'The Beacon'; the link from the name to 250 and 260 King St rests on the OpenStreetMap addr:housename tag cited in the geometry file and on SFHighrises and Afi + Associates, which both give 250 and 260 King St.
No construction start date or opening month found; the permit completed date is a closeout date, not an occupancy date.
The building permit for 260 King St has status 'reinstated' in the Department of Building Inspection data; the meaning is not explained in the data.

record.notes: Mixed-use condominium complex at 250 and 260 King St (the two OSM apartment-tagged building footprints tracked here); the Assessor parcel is condo-mapped across per-unit lots (DataSF Assessor parcel data). A broker's portfolio page (Afi + Associates, read 2026-09-29) describes a 'gourmet grocery store, bank, spa' at the complex; that is a secondary source and does not name the tenants. Architect attribution conflicts between sources (Afi + Associates says Skidmore, Owings and Merrill; earlier research also recorded Brand + Allen Architects and SOM/HKS from sources not cited here) and is not resolved -- not recorded as a fact pending a primary-source confirmation.
